analysis.title: CoreWeave (CRWV) 3Q26: Enjoy the GPUphoria while it lasts
key_insights: Bernstein maintains Underperform and a $54 price target on CRWV after what it calls about the best quarter it could have asked for. It cites execution and funding progress but long-term concerns about the business model.

The bull case requires three things: data center supply stays tight so pricing stays elevated, funding keeps getting easier, and CRWV reaches true hyperscale with self-funding, investment-grade economics. Bernstein doubts each.
CRWV is holding back 2028 capacity to wait for higher pricing, referencing $40M/MW. Bernstein is skeptical given an incremental 55GW+ announced across hyperscalers, neoclouds and SPCX through 2028.
Customer prepayments now run 15-50% of contract value on new deals, up from a 15-25% average at YE25. Bernstein doubts customers keep paying upfront once supply eases.

Q3 interest expense of $846M was more than 2x adjusted operating income of $379M. Debt rose $11.8B in the quarter to $46.9B against $4.0B of equity, and adjusted net income does not turn positive until 1H28.
Near-term, Bernstein sees a floor of $45-54 over the next few months, with possible upside to $64-73 if AI sentiment turns. The stock is off 65% from its May high.
Bernstein values CRWV at 22.5x EV/EBIT (previously 23.5x) and expects the October de-rating to be semi-permanent. The reasonable multiple range of 21.5-24.5x implies $45-74 near term.

Management expects less than $5B of incremental parent-level capital needs through 2027. Bernstein estimates total CapEx to deliver the full backlog is closer to $60B, versus FY26 CapEx of about $38B at the guidance midpoint.
3Q26 revenue was $3.66B, up 168% y/y and about 42% q/q, above the $3.45-3.60B guidance range. Backlog rose to $132.5B, up about 138% y/y and 27% q/q.

Adjusted operating income was $379M (10% margin), above the $200-260M guidance, reaching double-digit margins one quarter early. Management credited execution, stronger pricing and premium short-term contracts.

CRWV raised prices about 25% across SKUs in July and about another 10% later in the quarter, with pricing still rising in 4Q. Short-term opportunities run above $40M annual revenue per MW versus $20-25M for new 4-5 year contracts.
Active power reached more than 1.7GW versus about 1.5GW in 2Q, with the year-end target of more than 1.85GW maintained. Contracted power is 4.6GW, including more than 1.3GW outside the US.
Booked managed-inference ARR exceeded $250M, reaching the year-end target early. 70% of new cloud customers in 3Q were already Forge customers.

More than 130,000 GPUs come off contract in 2027 and about 170,000 in 2028. Management estimates nearly $4B of annualized revenue from the 2027 cohort and nearly $10B including 2028 at current pricing, outside reported backlog.

Bernstein's analysis puts the US data center pipeline near 75GW versus CRWV's 2-3GW, or about 55GW incremental after a credibility haircut. It says market-wide demand would have to multiply many times to keep pricing this tight.
The 35M-share ATM program implies stock-price impacts of -1.9% to -5.6%, all else equal. Bernstein says the ATM can remain a backstop if funding holds.
Weighted-average debt cost fell to 7.9%, down 250 bps y/y. Management expects the next DDTL to finance more than 90% of associated CapEx at an implied yield of 7.0-7.5%.
3Q26 CapEx was $14.5B per the text, above the $11.5-13.5B guidance, as deliveries were pulled forward from 4Q.

market_movers.rationale: Bernstein sees strong execution and funding progress but doubts pricing durability, funding and the path to hyperscale. It expects CRWV to be among the first and hardest hit as data center capacity eases.

sector_views.rationale: Bernstein expects data center supply to ease, which would pressure neocloud pricing and returns.

earnings_insights: CRWV 3Q26 reported revenue $3,661M vs Bernstein estimate $3,450M and consensus $3,555M, a 6.1% variance against Bernstein's forecast. Reported 3Q26.
CRWV 3Q26 adjusted operating income reported $379M (10.4% margin) vs Bernstein estimate $246M and consensus $246M. Company guidance was $200-260M.
CRWV 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA reported $2,256M (61.6% margin) vs Bernstein estimate $2,039M and consensus $2,050M.
CRWV 3Q26 adjusted diluted EPS reported $(0.95) vs Bernstein estimate $(0.88) and consensus $(1.21). GAAP diluted EPS was $(1.27) vs Bernstein estimate $(1.19) and consensus $(1.46).
CRWV 3Q26 GAAP operating income reported $207M vs Bernstein estimate $74M and consensus $64M. Net income was $(709)M vs Bernstein estimate $(663)M and consensus $(850)M.

CRWV 3Q26 CapEx is $14.5B in the report's narrative and $9,441M in the variance table, which conflict. The text says it was above the $11.5-13.5B guidance, and the variance table shows it below the Bernstein estimate of $10,896M.
CRWV 3Q26 free cash flow reported $(10,820)M vs Bernstein estimate $(14,565)M and consensus $(9,903)M.

CRWV FY26 guidance after 3Q26 (midpoints): revenue $13,150M (vs $12,800M after 2Q26, consensus $12,861M, Bernstein estimate $13,000M), adjusted operating income $1,325M (vs $1,230M), CapEx $38,000M (vs $37,000M).

Implied 4Q26 from guidance midpoints: revenue $4,836M (consensus $4,702M, Bernstein estimate $4,686M), adjusted operating income $797M (consensus $663M, Bernstein estimate $760M), interest expense about $1,100M, CapEx $7,300M.

Bernstein adjusted EPS estimates: FY26E $(3.54), up from $(5.14) prior, and FY27E $(3.20), up from $(6.60) prior. Note the report's income statement table shows FY27 adjusted diluted EPS of $(5.81), which conflicts with the $(3.20) cover figure.
risk_factors: Data center supply easing and new capacity (about 55GW incremental after haircut) could erode the premium pricing CRWV is seeing.
Customers may stop paying upfront prepayments once supply eases.
Interest expense (Q3 $846M) is more than 2x adjusted operating income, and debt rose $11.8B in a quarter to $46.9B.
Residual value of older-generation GPUs and the pricing of 2027-28 recontracting are key underwriting assumptions.
Short-duration contracts make current margins more sensitive to the supply-demand balance.
ATM dilution (up to 35M shares) and convertible-note financing add equity and financing risk.
The scale of the remaining buildout requires coordination across power, equipment, networking, cooling and financing.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots CRWV forward EV/adjusted EBIT with a 6-month average of 27.1x and Bernstein's 22.5x line.

Exhibit 2 shows a funding bridge: unrestricted cash $4.2B, construction in progress $9.3B, undrawn DDTL $5.0B and customer prepayments $9.0B against an estimated gap to fund of $32.5B and $60B total CapEx required for the backlog.
Exhibit 12 shows adjusted operating income of $379M versus interest expense of $846M in 3Q26.
vol_and_positioning: CRWV swings aggressively on newsflow and AI sentiment. The report lists a Nov 5 post-midterm AI selloff and Oct 16 bond yields above 16% as events in the multiple's path.
CRWV is down 32.0% YTD, 40.6% over 1M and 57.3% over 6M, and 63.9% relative to the SPX over 12M. It trades at 48.73 against a 52-week range of 40.58-138.25.
The CRWV EV/NTM adjusted EBIT multiple has a 6-month average of 27.1x, and a 120.3x max and 16.8x min over the longer weekly series. Bernstein uses 22.5x.

tension_points.bull_case: Qualified demand exceeds available capacity through 2027 by roughly 10x, pricing keeps rising (about 25% in July, about 10% more later in the quarter), adjusted operating margin reached 10% in 3Q, and prepayments plus secured debt cover funding needs with less than $5B of incremental parent-level capital through 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: About 55GW of incremental capacity is coming through 2028, upfront prepayments may fade once supply eases, interest expense is more than 2x adjusted operating income, and adjusted net income does not turn positive until 1H28.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Data center supply stays tight and spot pricing holds at or above the $20-25M/MW range implied for GPUs rolling off contract, which would support the bull case. Bernstein sees upside to $64-73 if AI sentiment turns.
